title: More pensions are tied to private credit, so more protection is necessary | World Economic Forum
gist: WEF argues post-2008 bank regulation pushed credit risk into private credit (FSB: $1.5-2tn; non-banks 51% of global financial assets), where judgement-based, infrequent valuations can hide losses that pension and insurance investors absorb. Citing HPS Corporate Lending Fund gating redemptions (11.5% requested vs 5% repurchased), the UK Mansion House Accord and ~$220bn of bank credit lines to private credit funds, it proposes an ESRB chain-wide stress test, valuation-transparency conditions and quarterly regulatory early-warning returns.

themes.theme: Post-2008 migration of credit risk to non-banks

insights.claim: Tighter bank rules after 2008 combined with low interest rates pushing investors to chase yield opened space for non-bank lenders; by end-2024 non-banks held 51% of global financial assets.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Credit risk has not disappeared post-2008 regulation, it has moved to less-supervised balance sheets.
insights.quote: By the end of 2024, non-banks held 51% of global financial assets.

insights.claim: The Financial Stability Board estimates the private credit market at $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion, with pension funds and insurers among its significant investors.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Private credit is now large enough that its stress transmits to retirement savings.
insights.quote: the Financial Stability Board (FSB) estimates private credit at $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion

insights.claim: Although post-crisis regulation may have made banks safer, risk persists in private credit and in its expanding links back to banks.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Bank-safety metrics understate system risk if non-bank channels are ignored.
insights.quote: while recent regulations may have made banks safer, risks remain in private credit and its growing connections with banks

insights.claim: Private loans rarely trade, so fund managers estimate their value; per the IMF, these valuations can be outdated and heavily dependent on judgement, meaning stress may only surface when assets are repriced.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Reported private credit NAVs likely lag true credit deterioration.
insights.quote: Private loans rarely trade, so fund managers estimate their value.

insights.claim: When fund withdrawals are priced off overstated asset values, departing investors are overpaid and remaining investors absorb the shortfall, creating a first-mover incentive.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Stale marks turn redemption queues into a wealth transfer from stayers to leavers.
insights.quote: Where withdrawals are priced using overstated asset values, departing investors can receive too much, leaving those who remain to bear the shortfall.
insights.locator: Fair valuations matter for all investors.

insights.claim: Defined-contribution savers, whose pots depend on investment performance, face the risk that delayed private credit losses crystallise just as they reach retirement.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Timing risk of deferred loss recognition falls hardest on near-retirees.
insights.quote: For defined-contribution savers, whose pension pots depend on investment performance, delayed losses could emerge just as they retire.

themes.theme: Redemption pressure at semi-liquid private credit funds

insights.claim: In September 2026 HPS Corporate Lending Fund, managed by BlackRock-owned HPS, received shareholder requests to sell back 11.5% of outstanding shares but said it would repurchase only 5%.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Redemption demand more than double the gate is a live stress signal in evergreen private credit vehicles.
insights.quote: reported shareholder requests to sell back 11.5% of its outstanding shares, but said it would repurchase only 5%

insights.claim: Repurchase limits avoid forced loan sales, but investors whose requests go unmet remain exposed to any subsequent change in the value of the fund.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Gates protect the fund but convert liquidity risk into trapped mark-to-model exposure for investors.
insights.quote: Such limits help avoid forced loan sales, but investors whose requests are not fully met must leave part of their money invested.

insights.claim: Many private credit funds lock investors in for years, which reduces withdrawal pressure and partly offsets run risk.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Lock-up structures are a genuine stabiliser versus bank-style runs.
insights.quote: many funds require investors to leave their money invested for years, reducing withdrawal pressures
insights.locator: Private credit can widen financing choices

themes.theme: Policy push of pensions into private markets

insights.claim: In 2025, 17 UK pension providers signed the Mansion House Accord, committing at least 10% of their main defined-contribution default funds to private markets by 2030.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Policy-driven flows will keep growing retail-pension exposure to opaque private assets.
insights.quote: In 2025, 17 UK pension providers signed the Mansion House Accord, committing at least 10% of their main defined-contribution default funds to private markets by 2030.

insights.claim: The FSB's May 2026 report identified about $220 billion in drawn and undrawn bank credit lines to private credit funds; small in aggregate, but a contagion channel where exposures are concentrated.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Concentrated bank lines to private credit funds are where spillovers would show first.
insights.quote: the FSB data identified around $220 billion in drawn and undrawn bank credit lines to private credit funds

insights.claim: A single borrower's distress can hit several institutions at once - a bank lending to the fund, plus pension and insurance investors in it - with loan agreements determining who absorbs losses first.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Loss waterfalls across the chain, not headline exposure, determine who gets hurt.
insights.quote: if the manufacturer struggles, any losses could affect several institutions, with loan agreements determining who bears the impact first

insights.claim: A European Central Bank exercise on euro area institutions found a severe shock could hit insurers and pension funds harder than banks, with the largest effects coming from assumed falls in wider markets rather than direct private credit losses, which looked manageable.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: The bigger danger is market-wide repricing transmitted via private credit holders, not loan defaults alone.
insights.quote: A European Central Bank exercise covering euro area institutions found that a severe shock could affect insurers and pension funds more than banks.

themes.theme: Regulatory proposals to protect pension savers

insights.claim: The European Systemic Risk Board should convene a voluntary pilot stress test with supervisors, banks, private credit funds, insurers and pension schemes - modelled on an ongoing Bank of England private markets exercise - mapping borrowers, lenders, investors and fund-level leverage under falling cash flows, higher rates and refinancing difficulty.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: An ESRB chain-wide stress test would reveal who bears losses and who needs cash.
insights.quote: The European Systemic Risk Board should convene a voluntary pilot with relevant supervisors, banks, private credit funds, insurers and pension schemes

insights.claim: Pension funds and insurers should make valuation transparency a condition of new investments, requiring managers to disclose valuation dates and the share by value independently reviewed in the past year, with missed payments or payment relief triggering prompt reassessment.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Independent-valuation coverage becomes a due-diligence screen for private credit allocations.
insights.quote: Managers should disclose when loans were valued and the share, by value, that received an independent valuation review in the past year

insights.claim: Private credit managers should file a standard quarterly return to regulators covering payment-in-kind interest, missed payments, loan extensions and fund leverage relative to investor capital, with regulators publishing aggregate trends and probing managers when they deteriorate.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: PIK usage, extensions and fund leverage are the key early-warning indicators to watch.
insights.quote: covering interest added to debt instead of paid in cash, missed payments, loan extensions and fund borrowing relative to investor capital
insights.locator: 3. Publish the warning lights and act on them
